label: The Twelve — Part 1 — Hoshea
summary_plain: Hoshea is commanded by YHWH to marry a woman of harlotry — Gomer — as a sign of Yisra'EL's unfaithfulness to YHWH. Their children are given names that are judgments: Yizre'el, Lo-Ruchamah (Not Pitied), Lo-Ammi (Not My People). But YHWH also promises restoration: 'I will say to Lo-Ammi — You are my people, and he shall say — You are my Creator.' YHWH declares: I will betroth you to me forever.
summary_scholarly: The ACR reads from the Minor Prophets Scroll (4QXII) at Qumran and the Orit Ge'ez. Hoshea is the first of the Twelve (Trei Asar). The marriage metaphor structures the entire book: YHWH as husband, Yisra'EL as unfaithful wife, the children's names as prophetic signs, and the ultimate restoration as remarriage. The judgment-restoration pattern in Hoshea parallels the Damascus Document's Period of Wrath followed by Period of Visitation.

key_terms.definition: Prophet in the northern kingdom; YHWH commanded him to marry Gomer as a living allegory of Yisra'el's unfaithfulness to the covenant.
Hoshea's marriage to Gomer, a woman of unfaithfulness, used by YHWH as a living picture of Yisra'el's covenant betrayal through idol worship.
YHWH's indictment: 'My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from being a priest to me.'
Prophet who interprets a devastating locust plague as a foretaste of the Day of YHWH and calls for communal repentance.
Yoel's central theme: a coming day of cosmic judgment and darkness, preceded by the locust invasion; the people are urged to return to YHWH before it arrives.
YHWH's promise: 'I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and daughters shall prophesy.' Ancient source text; the NT (Acts 2) borrowed from Yoel.
A herdsman and dresser of sycamore figs from Teqoa, called by YHWH to prophesy against Yisra'el's social injustice and hollow religious observance.
'But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.' YHWH rejects empty festivals while oppression persists.
YHWH stands with a plumb line beside a wall, measuring Yisra'el for structural failure; judgment is set and cannot be turned back.
'Are you not like the Kushim (Cushites) to me, O children of Yisra'el?' — YHWH establishes that covenant status does not make Yisra'el exempt from accountability.

faq.question: Who is Hoshea and what made his prophetic ministry unusual?
faq.answer: Hoshea was a prophet in the northern kingdom of Yisra'el. YHWH commanded him to marry a woman named Gomer and to have children with her as a living allegory — the marriage itself became the message, embodying how Yisra'el had abandoned the covenant relationship with YHWH for other gods.

faq.question: What is the central message of Hoshea 4:6?
faq.answer: YHWH declares that the people are being destroyed because they have rejected knowledge of YHWH and the covenant. This rejection is not ignorance but a deliberate turning away — the priests who should have taught the Torah abandoned their responsibility, so YHWH rejected them from the priestly function.

faq.question: Why is Hoshea 11:1 significant as an ancient source text?
faq.answer: Hoshea 11:1 reads 'Out of Mitzrayim I called my son,' referring to YHWH's redemption of Yisra'el from bondage. This ancient source text about Yisra'el's national history was later borrowed by NT writers who applied it to their invented figure — the direction of borrowing is from the ancient Hebrew text outward.

faq.question: What event prompted Yoel's prophetic message?
faq.answer: A devastating locust invasion that stripped the land bare became the occasion for Yoel's prophecy. He interpreted it as a foretaste of the coming Day of YHWH and called the entire community to genuine repentance — fasting, weeping, and returning to YHWH with their whole hearts.

faq.question: What does YHWH promise to do 'afterward' in Yoel 2:28?
faq.answer: YHWH promises to pour out the divine spirit on all flesh — sons, daughters, old and young, and servants alike will prophesy, see visions, and dream dreams. This ancient promise in Yoel became the source text the NT borrowed for its Pentecost narrative; Yoel is the original.

faq.question: Who was Amos and why was he an unexpected prophetic voice?
faq.answer: Amos was a herdsman and dresser of sycamore figs from Teqoa in the southern territory. He had no prophetic credentials or priestly lineage. YHWH took him from his agricultural work and sent him to the northern kingdom of Yisra'el to deliver a sharp indictment of its social injustice and hollow worship.

faq.question: What does Amos mean when he says YHWH rejects Yisra'el's festivals and assemblies?
faq.answer: In Amos 5:21-24, YHWH declares 'I hate, I despise your feasts' — not because festivals are wrong, but because the same community that gathered for religious observance was oppressing the poor, taking bribes, and denying justice. YHWH demanded that justice and righteousness flow like water before religious performance had any value.

faq.question: What does the plumb line vision in Amos 7 mean?
faq.answer: YHWH stands beside a wall holding a plumb line — a measuring instrument. YHWH is measuring Yisra'el against the straight standard of the covenant and finds it crooked beyond repair. The pronouncement is that YHWH will no longer pass over the structural failure; judgment is set.

faq.question: What is the significance of Amos 9:7 and the comparison to the Kushim?
faq.answer: YHWH asks Yisra'el: 'Are you not like the Kushim to me?' — meaning that covenant status does not create automatic exemption from YHWH's standards. YHWH governed the movements of other nations just as YHWH brought Yisra'el out of Mitzrayim. This text asserts YHWH's universal governance and rebukes national complacency.

faq.question: How does the locust imagery in Yoel relate to the Day of YHWH concept?
faq.answer: Yoel describes the locust invasion in terms that escalate into cosmic imagery — darkness, fire, an army without number. The locust plague is both a literal event and a living symbol of what the Day of YHWH will be like. YHWH uses the immediate crisis to call the people to return before the final Day arrives.
